Twenty-four little-endian screen row addresses, starting at $4400 and increasing by 40 to $4798. Several lookup routines add a calculated column to an address from this table and then adjust the high byte to address the grids at $F000 or $F400.

Compare $804A,X with $8041. When they differ, copy it to $8041, set $8042 to 0 for X other than 1 or 1 for X=1, call $86B6 with the matching value from $8026/$8027, then preserve X across a call to $8396. Set $8035,X to 1. On reaching 5, reset $803A, set $8037,X and the selected $801D,Y to 1. If $8025 is 4, set $8028 and switch the selected entry and screen using the other side; otherwise set $8041 to 0, call $8396, copy X to $8042, set $8056 to 1 and call $C9DB or $CA10 according to X.

Use A as the Y index into the two tables at $C674 and $C679. Write the results to $FC25,X and $FC26,X. For X=1, temporarily use X=2 for these stores and restore X=1 before returning. The selection update at $85B2 passes its five-step counter here.

If $FC25 is at least $A0, clear the motion origin and return. Otherwise, when $FE19 is nonzero, select sound effect $07 and clear the motion origin. If the $C00C entry indexed by $8026 is nonzero, toggle the motion mode and return. Increment $8714 and, on reaching $1A, reset it and call $C02C; if the voice 1 effect flag $E12F is clear, select effect $11. Choose a motion origin, copy $FC25 to $FE0B and dispatch values $60–$67 to eight separate routines; each recognized value then calls $8C7A and jumps to $8D0D. The purpose of each dispatched path remains to be traced.

Subtract $000C from $FC0B/$FC13 and $28 from $FC1B, then divide the low coordinate bytes by 8. Select a screen row through $8428, add the calculated column and, when the saved high X byte is nonzero, add $1F. Add $AC to the resulting high byte, plus 4 when $804A is nonzero, and read the patched address at $8CF7. If its value is 1, call $87E0; also call it if $FC1B is below $38. That helper clears $FC0B, $FC13 and $FC1B. The gameplay effect remains open.
Eight bytes added to the low X position at $FC05 by $FE30 after selecting a direction. The result and carry are stored at $FE12/$FE13.
Eight bytes added to the Y position at $FC15 by $FE30 after selecting a direction. The routine subtracts 8 and stores the result at $FE14.

Return unless $804A,X equals $804D. Convert the two-byte position at $8047/$8048 to a half-width value. Search the eight bytes at $9620 for the pointer at $FC25,Y. On a match, replace that pointer with the byte at the same index in $9618; return unchanged when no entry matches.

Save Y on the stack, set $99C1 to 3 and copy $804A,X to $804D. Read $FC16,Y into $8049, substituting $D2 for $CF, $D0 or $D1; copy $FC06,Y/$FC0E,Y to $8047/$8048 and subtract $10. Save this address at $99C6/$99C7 and its value plus $28 at $99CC/$99CD. Patch the reads at $97E9 and $9835 to this address. If $9486 is nonzero, clear it and return. Otherwise toggle $948A. When setting it, call $871B; when clearing it, call $FE96 if $FE19 is nonzero. The gameplay role of $948A remains open.

If $9486 is nonzero, clear it and return. Otherwise select the first zero flag among $949D–$949F; if none is zero, return. Copy the three state bytes at $9499, $949A and $949B to $FC0B,X, $FC13,X and $FC1B,X, respectively. The caller chooses X. This runs before each directional update, so these destinations receive the previous state.

Publish the prior position, set $FC2B,X to $7E, and add 10 to the little-endian value at $9499/$949A. If the high byte is nonzero and the low byte is at least $60, clear the selected flag.
